1:13: literally, “gird up the waist of your mind” or “put on the belt of the waist of your mind”
2:6: “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה” or “ἰδοὺ”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.
2:25: “Overseer” is from the Greek episkopon, which can mean overseer, curator, guardian, or superintendent.
